title: ASP.NET Core Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: MapGet connects a GET path to a function. Open GET /. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: MapGet matches the root GET request. Its function returns the greeting string. MapGet only handles matching GET requests.

exercises.question: Results.Json sends structured data as JSON. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Results.Json serialises the anonymous object with the named fields. Use objects for data instead of joining JSON text by hand.

exercises.question: Curly braces name a route value. Open GET /hello/Ravi. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Route binding supplies Ravi to the string input. The interpolated string uses that value. Do not place user text into raw HTML without escaping it.

exercises.question: The int route constraint only matches whole numbers. Open GET /double/4. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The int constraint matches 4. Binding supplies an int and the handler doubles it. A failed route constraint usually means this route does not match.

exercises.question: A simple input outside the path can come from the query string. GET /page with no n uses the fallback. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The nullable query input is absent. The ?? expression supplies 1. A missing optional number is null, not automatically zero.

exercises.question: A record can describe body data. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The JSON body is bound to a Book record. Results.Json sends its Title in the web JSON naming style. A type describes shape; add checks for values that must not be empty.

exercises.question: The handler checks a title before returning a created response. Send POST /books with {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The title passes the whitespace check. Created returns the book with status 201 and a location. Minimal APIs in this version do not make every custom validation rule for you.

exercises.question: Middleware can run before and after later handlers. GET /note carries the header set here. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The middleware adds Cache-Control, then awaits the next handler. That handler supplies the note. Call next when the request should continue through the pipeline.

exercises.question: MapGroup gives several routes one common prefix. Open GET /api/books. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The group prefix and inner path combine to /api/books. The string array becomes JSON. The group prefix is part of each final route.

exercises.question: A registered service can be an input to a handler. Open GET /school. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The service is registered before Build. Handler injection supplies its SchoolName instance. Register services before building the app.

exercises.question: Results.NotFound gives a 404 response. Open GET /missing. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Results.NotFound includes both the 404 status and a serialised error object. Use the error status as well as a helpful message.

exercises.question: Results.Redirect sends a location. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The redirect response points to /hello. The follow-up GET receives Welcome. A redirect asks the client to make a second request.
